_comment: Source for scripts/solve_games.py. Payoffs are ordinal, chosen so each game has its canonical structure. Equilibria are computed, never typed here.

games.name: Prisoner's Dilemma
games.life: Trust with someone you may not deal with again
games.reading: Defecting pays more whatever the other player does. Both defect and receive 1, though mutual cooperation would give each player 3.
games.move: Make the relationship repeat. When the future matters enough, conditional cooperation becomes rational.

games.name: Stag Hunt
games.life: Cofounders, marriage, any ambitious joint bet
games.reading: Hunting stag pays more when both commit. Hare pays less but remains safe when the other person wavers. Doubt drives this game.
games.move: Buy assurance before you commit. Evidence that they will show up is worth more than a better offer.

games.name: Chicken
games.life: Ego standoffs, brinkmanship, who blinks first
games.reading: Two equilibria, and in each one somebody swerves. The crash is worst for both, which is exactly why the threat works.
games.move: Build a face-saving exit for them. Cornering someone in Chicken raises your odds of the crash.

games.name: Trust Game
games.reading: Sending creates value only if it comes back. Backward induction says they keep, so you never send, and the surplus is never made.
games.move: Send a small amount first. Escalate on evidence, not on how trustworthy they sound.

games.name: Public Goods
games.life: Housework, team effort, anything everyone benefits from
games.reading: Everyone wants the shared good and would prefer someone else to fund it. Free-riding dominates, so the good stays underfunded.
games.move: Make each contribution visible. People often free-ride on work they cannot see.

games.name: Coordination
games.life: Two good options, and being together beats being right
games.reading: You each prefer a different option, but a mismatch pays nobody. Both matching outcomes are stable.
games.move: Agree a focal point in advance, or alternate. Arguing over which is better wastes the surplus you are arguing about.

games.name: Matching Pennies
games.life: Genuinely adversarial: bluffing, bidding, tactical surprise
games.reading: No pure equilibrium exists. Any pattern you settle into can be exploited, so stable play requires unpredictability.
games.move: Reserve zero-sum tactics for genuinely adversarial games. Applied elsewhere, they burn value both sides could have kept.

games.name: Principal-Agent
games.life: Managing, delegating, hiring anyone whose effort you cannot see
games.reading: Monitoring is costly and can damage trust. Without it, hidden effort invites shirking. The problem begins with poor visibility.
games.move: Make the outcome observable and reward it directly. Better evidence reduces the need to police behaviour.

levers.ask: Who is at the table, and who could be?
levers.example: Negotiating harder will not fix a poor choice of cofounder. Change who is at the table.

viz.after: Change who is at the table
viz.cap: Change who is at the table.

levers.ask: What is each person rewarded for?
levers.example: If comp rewards beating colleagues, no amount of asking for collaboration will produce it.

viz.cap: Collaboration follows the reward structure.

levers.ask: Who knows what, and what stays hidden?
levers.example: Mistrust often means low observability. Make the work visible before appealing to good faith.

viz.cap: Mistrust often means low observability.

levers.ask: Who moves first, and can that change?
levers.example: Split one irreversible commitment into stages and each stage buys information for the next.

viz.cap: Split one irreversible commitment into stages.

levers.ask: Which constraints are real, and which come from habit?
levers.example: Constant interruptions point to a bad protocol. Change the protocol so you stop absorbing the cost.

viz.cap: The protocol keeps producing the interruption.

levers.ask: Is this the right place to be playing at all?
levers.example: In a commodity market everyone competes on price. Differentiate, or find a market where you are scarce.

viz.mine: A market where you are scarce
viz.cap: Differentiate, or move.

levers.ask: What happens if you walk, and how good is that?
levers.example: Your bargaining power is set before the negotiation by how survivable no-deal is.

viz.beyond: Anything you say at the table
viz.cap: Bargaining power is set before the negotiation.

laws.why: Nothing compounds after ruin. Expected value stops being the right measure once a loss ends your ability to keep playing.

viz.cap: Nothing compounds after ruin.

laws.why: The same people come back. That is what makes reputation an asset and betrayal expensive.

viz.cap: The same people come back.

laws.why: Treating a joint problem as a contest destroys the surplus you were both there to create.

viz.cap: Treating a joint problem as a contest destroys it.

laws.why: One promotion, one contract, one auction. Misreading these as cooperative is its own kind of loss.

viz.cap: Some games really are fixed.

laws.why: Evaluate a decision after everyone else has replied to it.

viz.cap: Evaluate after everyone has replied.

laws.law: Change the game before playing harder
laws.why: Effort inside a badly structured game is the most expensive way to lose.

viz.cap: Effort inside a bad game is expensive.

laws.why: Under uncertainty, a cheap experiment is usually worth more than a confident decision.

viz.cap: Under uncertainty, information is worth more.

laws.why: Small bet, then evidence, then large bet. Reversing that order is how people lose big.

viz.cap: Reversing that order is how people get hurt.

laws.law: Exclude sunk cost from the next decision
laws.why: What you already spent is a fact about the past. Compare only the future costs and benefits you can still change.

viz.cap: Compare the future costs and benefits.

laws.why: Bargaining power is built before the conversation, by making no-deal survivable.

viz.cap: Power is built before the conversation.

laws.why: It takes years to build and one transaction to spend. Price it accordingly.

viz.cap: It rebuilds far slower than it breaks.

laws.why: When the stated goal and the reward structure disagree, the reward structure wins.

viz.cap: When they disagree, the rewards win.

laws.law: Avoid success that costs you agency
laws.why: A well-paid role you cannot leave is a trap that looks like an achievement.

viz.cap: A trap that looks like an achievement.

laws.why: Ask whether today's choice improves the sequence of states that follows.

viz.cap: Ask what today improves downstream.

laws.why: Spend less of your life in games where winning gives you nothing you value.

viz.theirs: Games where winning costs too much
viz.cap: Spend less time in games where winning costs too much.

dashboard.ask: Is my capability growing along with my responsibility?
Do I capture upside from the value I create?
Does home restore energy or consume it?
Am I deciding from equilibrium or from strain?
Am I gaining useful future options?
Are more of these relationships built on trust?
Are my claims backed by evidence?
Does my authority match my responsibility?
Would I value this life with no spectators?
Do I have more credible moves than a year ago?

classifier.q: Who are the players, including future you?
classifier.why: Present you and future you have different incentives and rarely negotiate.
Compare what they say with the choices they repeatedly make.
Order determines who commits and who responds, and often decides the outcome.
One-shot and repeated versions of the same game have opposite correct strategies.
Zero-sum tactics can destroy value when both sides could have gained.
Hidden information is where most bad deals are made.

classifier.q: What happens if I refuse to play?
classifier.why: Your no-deal outcome sets your bargaining power before you say anything.
Reversible decisions reward speed. Irreversible ones reward patience.
The move that fails is usually the one that assumed nobody would react.

five.ask: What do they do after I move?
five.note: This is the visible game. It matters, though the other four layers may shape the decade more.

viz.cap: The visible game.

five.ask: Can we make more together than apart?
five.note: Much of life's value is made with other people. Treating every shared problem as a contest destroys some of that value.

viz.cap: Much of life’s value is made with other people.

five.ask: What am I committing my future self to?
five.note: Your future selves cannot object to choices you make for them today. Debt, habits, contracts and specialisation all belong to this layer.

viz.cap: Your future selves are players too.

five.ask: What survives if the draw goes badly?
five.note: Nature is indifferent. Build plans that can survive bad timing, illness and an unlucky draw.

viz.cap: Nature is indifferent.

five.vs: The choice of which game to enter
five.ask: Why am I playing this one at all?
five.note: This layer lets you question the frame itself. Choosing a better game can matter more than improving your play.

viz.cap: This layer questions the frame itself.

domains.winning: Capability that is hard to replace, with results other people can verify.
domains.risk: Becoming indispensable in a role that creates no bargaining power. Praise rises while outside options stay flat.
domains.ask: Does my future bargaining power grow with this responsibility?
domains.math: Skill → Scarcity → Evidence → Bargaining Power → Choice

viz.cap: Scarcity matters when it improves your options.

domains.winning: Pay that grows with judgement, scarcity or ownership. Hours worked become less important.
domains.risk: One employer, one client, one credential. Dependency turns a good income into a fragile one.
domains.ask: What mechanism decides what this can eventually pay?
domains.math: Income ∝ Hours → Income ∝ Judgement, Scarcity, Ownership

viz.cap: Dependency makes a good income fragile.

domains.winning: Staying in the game long enough for returns to compound.
domains.risk: Position sizes that carry real ruin risk. One bad sequence and the compounding stops.
domains.ask: If the downside lands at the worst moment, am I still playing?
domains.math: W<sub>t+1</sub> = W<sub>t</sub>(1 + r) − C  subject to  P(ruin) < ε

viz.cap: One bad sequence ends the compounding.

domains.winning: Holding a claim on value you helped create and sharing in the upside.
domains.risk: Entering because ownership sounds like freedom, without a customer or an unfair advantage.
domains.ask: What happens if this works and the incumbent responds rationally?

viz.cap: Verify the customer and the advantage first.

domains.winning: A relationship in which conflict can be repaired reliably.
domains.risk: Treating it as zero-sum. Winning the argument while lowering the value of the relationship.
domains.ask: Does repeated interaction here increase trust and capability, or steadily reduce them?

viz.cap: Treating it as zero-sum lowers both.

domains.winning: Contributions and authority made explicit, so the load does not silently fall on one person.
domains.risk: Free-riding on invisible labour. Nobody intends it, and the structure produces it anyway.
domains.ask: Is this a character problem or an incentive problem?

viz.cap: Nobody intends it; the structure produces it.

domains.winning: A smaller set of trusted relationships can be worth more than a large contact list. These people would still take your call without the job titles.
domains.risk: Treating a network as something to extract from. People remember that behaviour.
domains.ask: Am I contributing here, or only withdrawing?

viz.cap: People remember extraction.

domains.winning: Signals that are expensive to fake. Shipped work, kept promises, consistent judgement.
domains.risk: Spending a decade of trust on one transaction. It rebuilds far slower than it breaks.
domains.ask: Could someone without the underlying capability afford to send this signal?
domains.math: T<sub>t+1</sub> = (1 − ρ)T<sub>t</sub> + aR<sub>t</sub> − bD<sub>t</sub>,   b > a

viz.cap: It compounds and decays asymmetrically.

domains.winning: Responsibility, authority and accountability roughly in balance.
domains.risk: Responsibility far exceeding authority. You absorb the blame for outcomes you cannot control.
domains.ask: Am I being given power, or only exposure?

viz.cap: You absorb blame for outcomes you cannot control.

domains.winning: Knowledge that transfers, compounds, and eventually changes what you do.
domains.risk: Consuming information because it feels productive, without using it to change a decision or action.
domains.ask: Can I use this yet, or have I only read about it?

viz.cap: It feels productive either way.

domains.winning: Work at the intersection of genuine curiosity and non-generic knowledge.
domains.risk: Optimising novelty without usefulness, or usefulness without distinctiveness.
domains.ask: Which term in the product is closest to zero?

viz.cap: Both halves are required.

domains.winning: Confidence built through evidence, repetition and recovery.
domains.risk: Outsourcing your sense of self to recognition. Praise then sets your direction, and so does criticism.
domains.ask: Does repeating this make me more capable, or only more approved of?

viz.cap: Praise then sets your direction.

domains.winning: Deciding from equilibrium. Recognising which internal player currently holds the pen.
domains.risk: Local relief that raises the future cost. Avoidance and overwork both do this.
domains.ask: Which version of me is making this call, and on what horizon?

viz.cap: Local relief raises the future cost.

domains.winning: Sources of meaning that do not depend on outranking anyone.
domains.risk: Rank-based satisfaction. The reference group climbs with you and the target keeps moving.
domains.ask: Would I value this with no spectators?

viz.beyond: A reference group that climbs with you
viz.cap: The target keeps moving.

domains.winning: An environment that amplifies you. No location is good in the abstract.
domains.risk: Committing permanently on holiday data. A visit and a life are different samples.
domains.ask: What version of me does this place encourage?

viz.cap: A visit gives weak evidence about daily life.

domains.winning: Recovery scheduled as part of the work, including when the work remains unfinished.
domains.risk: Every domain withdrawing from one biological account with nobody governing the withdrawals.
domains.ask: Is this replenishing energy or borrowing it from tomorrow?

viz.cap: Nobody is governing the account.

domains.winning: Output that remains sustainable for years.
domains.risk: Converting a temporary biological capacity into a permanent expectation.
domains.ask: Is the current pace something I could hold for a decade?

viz.cap: A temporary capacity becomes permanent expectation.

regimes.when: Evidence is strong and the environment rewards scale.
regimes.avoid: Hedging so heavily you cannot press the advantage

viz.theirs: Hedging so heavily you cannot press
viz.cap: Evidence is strong; press it.

regimes.when: Uncertainty is high and commitments are still reversible.

viz.cap: Commitments are still reversible.

regimes.when: Growth outran the systems holding it up.
regimes.avoid: Adding new fronts before the current one is stable

viz.cap: Growth outran the systems holding it up.

regimes.when: Downside risk has risen or the ground is moving.

viz.cap: Protect solvency while downside risk is rising.

regimes.when: Capacity is depleted and judgement is degraded.

viz.cap: Judgement is degraded.

regimes.when: The current game no longer fits, but the next is unbuilt.
regimes.avoid: Burning the boat before the alternative exists

viz.cap: The next game is unbuilt.

readiness.body: You have little capacity and few good openings. Rebuild the base before forcing a move.
readiness.rule: Protect resources. Stop the bleeding first.

readiness.body: You are ready, but the environment offers little. Use the quiet period to prepare.
readiness.rule: Build skill, network and runway now. The opening arrives on its own schedule.

readiness.body: A real opening has arrived before you are ready. Take part at a size the whole system can survive.
readiness.rule: Capture upside at small size. Learn fast.

readiness.body: Readiness and opportunity have arrived together. This combination is rare and may not last.
readiness.rule: Concentrate enough effort to use the opening while it exists.
